submitted.rationale: EQE falls steadily as Sb increases: 0.162% at idx 0 (Fe0.87), 0.106% at idx 3 (Fe0.82), about 0 at idx 14 (FeSbO4). XRD shows a rutile FeSbO4-type phase across the whole line. The best photoresponse is at the most Fe-rich end, which is consistent with hematite-like Fe-rich absorption at 2.1 eV.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE ~0 even though MEGNet predicts a 2.08 eV gap and MACE puts FeSbO4 on the hull
EQE decreases with more Sb, and the Sb-rich FeSb2O4 phase is predicted to have a 2.38 eV gap, above the photon energy

consultations.verdict: Support: rutile FeSbO4 is on hull (0.002 eV/atom) with HSE-level gap 2.08 eV, just under 2.1 eV photon energy, so it absorbs; Fe2O3 predicted 2.77 eV (MEGNet overestimate) is less favorable. Index 14 (Fe0.52Sb0.48) is closest to FeSbO4 stoichiometry.

Mixed but supports trying the Fe-rich end: Fe2O3 is on hull (MACE) and experimentally ~2.1 eV gap, while Sb-rich FeSb2O4 is predicted 2.38 eV (above 2.1 eV photons) -> Sb-rich side disfavored. FeSbO4 at index 14 gave ~0 EQE, so pivot to the most Fe-rich composition where hematite-like absorption/Fe excess may help.

Uninformative: SCAN-fidelity MEGNet gap for Fe2O3 (0.81 eV) conflicts with the HSE value and does not discriminate among Fe-rich compositions. Decision rests on data: EQE rises strongly toward Fe-rich (0.16% at idx 0 vs ~0 at idx 14); probe idx 3 to test for an interior optimum near the Fe-rich end while staying in the high-mean region.
